title: Clamp decal and area light atlases to the maximum 2D texture size

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
During my recent playtest, some playtesters discovered an issue where nothing but the sky was being rendered, and their logs were filled with RenderingDevice errors. Upon investigation I found that the maximum texture size supported by their GPUs was not large enough for the decal atlas being created (I have a lot of decals). I reduced my own decal resolutions, but also worked on a fix in the engine so it wouldn't happen again, because it makes sense to me that the engine should not allow this, and other users might run in to the same issue and could instead benefit from this change.

Changes:
The decal and area light atlases grow their width and height unbounded as unique texture content is added. Once an atlas exceeds the device's maximum 2D texture size, texture_create() fails and the atlas can no longer be built, flooding the log with RenderingDevice errors and breaking decal/area light rendering.

Clamp each atlas to RD::LIMIT_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE_2D. When the content would overflow that cap, halve every item and re-pack at a lower resolution. The atlas blit already scales each source into its uv_rect, so downscaled entries still render. Emit a one-time warning when this happens.

The near-identical packing loops in both functions are extracted into a shared _pack_atlas_items() helper, to reduce some existing code duplication.

Use of AI must be disclosed and should include a description of how it was used.
--> AI was used to pinpoint the issue in my games crash logs from the playtester that had the issue.

## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- A crash in my own game, where generated decal texture atlas size was larger than the GPUs maximum supported size.

## Additional information
This is my first contribution, so I am more than happy to fix any stylistic issues or anything, or revert my removal of the duplicated code if it was done for reasons i dont understand. e.g. "Observe the code you are changing, and avoid changing it to suit your own personal preferences unless there is a tangible benefit." - I think code duplication goes beyond personal preference, but again happy to revert.
